evaluations.label: A
errors: "Alternative: recess or offset channel buttons slightly" - 'recess' is an embellishment; the UI designer only said to put the channel numbers a bit out of the way
"Backlit buttons confirmed" overstates it; the lighting was debated and set aside ('we will discuss that after'), only referenced again later by the PM

Next steps split into separate per-person tasks ('Industrial designer to produce final banana-form design', 'UI designer to finalize layout') that the PM did not assign individually; he asked both to work together
strengths: Accurate recap of previous meeting decisions
Captures the key numbers (wheel sensor ~50x a push button, 12 euro limit) and the reason the wheel was kept
Clearly records voice-recognition chip email and that the decision was deferred
Covers the light activation debate and battery concern, the plastic-cover reversal, banana choice with reasons, spongy cover construction, left/right-hand discussion
weaknesses: Some items labeled as 'confirmed' or decisions were looser in the meeting
No timestamps; does not mention that further instructions will come by email

evaluations.label: B
errors: "IS1001c remote control" - this identifier never appears in the transcript
"backlit buttons that activate upon movement" stated as a specification; the motion sensor was objected to as too expensive and not decided
"an arched internal structure for component mounting" - not said; the PM said 'odd shaped, with a spongy cover'
"spongy material for robustness and tactile appeal" - 'tactile appeal' not mentioned
"Action Items (none)" contradicts the PM asking the industrial and UI designers to work together on the prototype
Uses 'UIZ' as a role name, which is not in the transcript
strengths: Good narrative summary plus a chronological outline
Captures wheel cost (50x), 12 euro budget, voice chip, plastic cover rejection, wheel push-down, banana choice with reasons
Useful 'unresolved questions' section (voice chip, lighting cost, spongy case vs button presses)
weaknesses: Action items section is empty even though the collaboration task was given
Generic 'Speaker 1/2/3/4' labels make attribution hard to follow
Several small invented details and overstated decisions

evaluations.label: C
errors: "a channel wheel, preview button" - it was a previous-channel button, not a preview button
"The group kept the wheel ... [11:04]" - at that point the PM only said 'maybe'; the decision to keep it came later (~15:54)
"The group did not document a detailed resolution" on left/right handedness understates that the PM argued it works for both hands and the UI designer accepted ('Okay. Maybe.')
strengths: Timestamps make claims easy to check
Correct coverage of wheel cost, 12 euro target, light debate and battery concern, plastic-cover concern, voice chip with 'no decision', market priorities in order
Clearly states the final concept (yellow banana, wheel on top, buttons on side, spongy cover, standard battery, chip-on-print)
Records the designers' joint prototype work, next tasks and that instructions will come by email
weaknesses: Empty 'Action items' heading at the end
Some repetition between the summary and body sections
Does not record that the previous plastic-cover decision was effectively dropped

evaluations.label: D
errors: "Heart-shaped core with spongy cover suggested" - the PM said 'odd shaped' with a spongy cover
"UI Designer (UL Hazred)" - the name given was Abdul al-Hasred
"Facilitate discussion on wheel sensor necessity" and "Assess cost implications of wheel sensor" are invented action items; the wheel was decided to be kept
"Banana shape proposed" understates that the banana was chosen
"Simple remote interface confirmed" lists previous-meeting decisions as if made in this meeting, and omits the plastic cover and no-LCD/no-voice items
Several timestamps do not match the transcript (e.g. 'Provide meeting notes in shared folder (00:00)')
strengths: Captures 50x wheel cost and 12 euro budget
Notes plastic-cover concerns, motion-sensor cost, spongy-case concern and banana/yellow/company colors
Has an action item section split by role
weaknesses: Omits the voice-recognition chip email entirely
Omits battery consumption concern, standard battery and chip decisions
Action items partly invented and repetitive
Decisions (keep wheel, banana chosen) stated weakly

rationale: A is the most complete and accurate, with clear decisions, deferred items and next steps, only minor overstatements. C is accurate and well grounded with timestamps but has the 'preview button' error, an empty action items heading and slightly weaker decision framing. B has a good outline and open questions but invents details (IS1001c, arched structure, motion-activated backlight as a spec) and lists no action items. D omits the voice chip, mis-transcribes 'odd shaped' as 'heart-shaped', misspells the name, and invents wheel-cost action items after the wheel was kept.
